item.title: Eight Students from Assam Trek 15 Km to Exam Centre as Village Has No Motorable Road
item.description: GUWAHATI: The Class 10 board examinations began across Assam on February 11, with over 4 lakh students appearing in 2026. Among them are eight students from Mualdam, a remote village in Dima Hasao district, who have to trek fifteen kilometres through hilly terrain to appear for their examinations, marking the first time their school has sent a batch for the HSLC exam. item.title: CNG Shortage at Paltan Bazar Brings Traffic Chaos to Guwahati Roads
item.description: Drivers wait hours for CNG as supply crisis worsens Long lines of vehicles stretching across key roads in Guwahati have become a daily sight near Manipuri Basti in Paltan Bazar, where one of the few CNG refill stations operated by Purba Bharti Gas Private Limited (PBGPL) is located. What was once projected as a step towards cleaner fuel and a less polluted Guwahati is now, for many commuters and drivers, turning into hours of waiting, traffic snarls and growing frustration. item.title: MMCH Super-Speciality Hospital Held Back by Power Bottleneck
item.description: A mega healthcare upgrade meant to ease pressure on Guwahati Medical College and Hospital faces delays, leaving patients frustrated Guwahati's Mahendra Mohan Choudhury Hospital (MMCH), situated in the Pan Bazar area, functioned as a multi-disciplinary extension of the Guwahati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH). The hospital has been closed since January 2022 to undergo a drastic transformation. The hospital, originally built in 2013, catered to a large number of patients from across the city.

item.description: Encroachments and parking push Guwahati pedestrians onto busy roads Pedestrians in Guwahati are increasingly being forced off footpaths and onto busy roads as sidewalks across key commercial areas are occupied by street vendors, parked two-wheelers, makeshift extensions of shops, and in several places, broken slabs and open manholes. item.description: GUWAHATI: The Gauhati High Court has permitted the Assam government to proceed with limited preparatory and ancillary work under the ₹498-crore Kamakhya Corridor project, while firmly directing that the main shrine remain untouched.
